correctness.rationale: After phase normalization, exact maximization in w reduces the norm to F(z)=|A+Bz|+|C+D e^{i phi}z|. Evaluating at the antipodal points z=+/-e^{-i phi/2}, the sum of the two squared values is bounded below by (A+B+C+D)^2 using a single triangle inequality; hence one value is at least the coefficient mass divided by sqrt(2). The polynomial 1+z+w-zw has norm exactly 2sqrt(2), so the constant is sharp. Zero-coefficient boundary cases follow by continuity. The standalone verifier checks the decisive two-sample inequality numerically on deterministic random data but is not used as proof.

value.rationale: The result gives an exact four-frequency Sidon constant in the first Cartesian rectangle geometry, with a short structural certificate that exploits the two-variable product phase. Exact four-frequency Sidon constants are nontrivial: the one-variable set {0,1,2,3} remains unresolved in current literature. The statement is not a routine numerical recomputation or parameter increment; it isolates a tractable multivariable geometry and gives a sharp constant plus an explicit extremizer.
